title: Underwriting Guidelines: Open Owner Auto Policy Terms per Named Insured
content:
**Rule.** A named insured may hold at most 2 Owner Auto Policy terms that are open at the same time. The maximum of 2 open terms is a company figure that applies on every package.

**What counts as open.**
- A term is open while its status is bound, in force or pending cancellation.
- A renewal offer on a policy number that already has an open term does not count separately, because it replaces that term on its effective date.
- Expired, cancelled and not-taken terms never count.

**Second policies.** A second policy is written only for vehicles principally garaged at a different address of the named insured. Vehicles garaged at the same address are scheduled on the existing policy.

**Eligibility for new business.** The named insured must not already hold the maximum number of open Owner Auto Policy terms. This is read from the company's policy records for that named insured, before the new business is bound. An application beyond the maximum is declined, and the vehicles are offered as an addition to an open policy instead.

| Open terms already held | New-business application |
|---|---|
| 0 or 1 | may proceed (subject to the other rules) |
| 2 | declined; the vehicles are offered as an addition to an open policy |

**Example (hypothetical).** A named insured holds one in-force term and one expired term. Only the in-force term is open, so a new application for vehicles garaged at a different address is not barred by this rule.
